questions.q: If the coefficients of $x^3$ and $x^4$ in the expansion of $\left(1+a x+b x^2\right)(1-2 x)^{18}$ in powers of $x$ are both zero, then $(a, b)$ is equal to
questions.solution:
In the expansion of $\left(1+a x+b x^2\right)(1-2 x)^{18}$ coefficient of $x^3$ in $\left(1+a x+b x^2\right)(1-2 x)^{18}=$ Coefficient of $x^3$ in $(1-2 x)^{18}+$ coefficient of $x^2$ in $a(1-2 x)^{18}+$ coefficient of $x$ in $b(1-2 x)^{18}$.
$=-{ }^{18} C_3 \cdot 2^3+a^{18} C_2 \cdot 2^2-b^{18} C_4 \cdot 2\because \quad-{ }^{18} C_3 \cdot 2^3+a^{18} C_2 \cdot 2^2-b^{18} C_4 \cdot 2=0\Rightarrow \frac{18 \times 17 \times 16}{3 \times 2} \cdot 8+a \cdot \frac{18 \times 17}{2} 2^2-b \cdot 18 \cdot 2=0\Rightarrow 17 a-b=\frac{34 \times 16}{3}\ldots$ (i)
Similarly, coefficient of $x^4{ }^{18} C_4 \cdot 2^4-a \cdot{ }^{18} C_3 2^3+b \cdot{ }^{18} C_2 \cdot 2^2=0\therefore \quad 32 a-32 b=240\ldots$ (ii)
From Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get
$a=16$ and $b=\frac{272}{3}$

$\because(9)^{50}=(10-1)^{50}\begin{aligned} &=\left[{ }^{50} C_0(10)^{50}(-1)^0-{ }^{50} C_1(10)^{49}(1)\right.+\ldots .]-\binom{50}{49}(10)^1 \\ &+\binom{50}{50}(10)^0\end{aligned}\because$ All the terms in the bracket are multiples of $10^2$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The differential equation of all circles which pass through the origin and whose centres lies on $Y$-axis is
questions.solution:
The equation of family of circles which passess through the origin and whose centrer lies on $Y$-axis is $(x-0)^2+(y-k)^2=k^2\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow x^2+y^2+k^2-2 y k=k^2 \\ & \Rightarrow x^2+y^2-2 y k=0\end{aligned}$
where, $k$ is parameter.
On differentiating w.r.t . $x$, we get
$2 x+2 y \frac{d y}{d x}-2 \frac{d y}{d x} k=0\begin{array}{ll}\Rightarrow & x+(y-k) \frac{d y}{d x}=0 \\ \Rightarrow & x+\left\{y-\frac{x^2+y^2}{2 y}\right\} \frac{d y}{d x}=0\end{array}
$\begin{array}{ll}\Rightarrow & x+\frac{1}{2 y}\left(y^2-x^2\right) \frac{d y}{d x}=0 \\ \Rightarrow & 2 x y=\left(x^2-y^2\right) \frac{d y}{d x}\end{array}
$\Rightarrow \quad \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{2 x y}{x^2-y^2}$,
which is required equation.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If complex number $z$ lies in the interior or on the boundary of circle of radius 3 units, then maximum and minimum values of $|z+1|$ are
questions.solution: Here, we have Radius of circle $=3$ units we find the maximum and minimum value of $|z+1|$ for $z$ lying in the interier or boundary of the circle $|z|=3$ For $\operatorname{Max}|z+1|, z$ must lies on the bondary of the circle, then $|z|=3$ and $z=3 e^\theta$, where $\theta$ is the argument of $z$. Now, $|z+1|=\left|3 e^{i \theta}+1\right|\begin{aligned} & =|(3 \cos \theta+1)+(3 i \sin \theta)| \\ & =\sqrt{(3 \cos \theta+1)^2+(3 \sin \theta)^2}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =\sqrt{9+1+6 \cos \theta} \\ & =\sqrt{10+6 \cos \theta}\end{aligned}\sin \theta, \cos \theta$ ranges from -1 to 1 , the maximum value of $|z+1|$ occur, when $\cos \theta=1$. Therefore, $\operatorname{Max}|z+1|=\sqrt{10+6}=\sqrt{16}=4$ For minimum value The minimum value of $z+1$ occures, when $z$ is at the centre of the circle $|z|=3$. In this case $z=0$. On putting $z=0$ into the expression, we have $\operatorname{Min}(|z+1|)=|0+1|=1$ Hence, maximum value of $|z+1|=4$ minimum value of $|z+1|=1$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $f(x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+x^2}}$, then
questions.solution:
Given that
$f(x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+x^2}}\therefore \quad f(y)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+y^2}}$
and $f(x, y)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+x^2 y^2}}$
Now, $f(x, y)=f(x) \cdot f(y)\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+x^2 y^2}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+x^2}} \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{1+y^2}}\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+x^2 y^2}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\left(1+x^2\right)\left(1+y^2\right)}}$
On squaring both sides, we get
$\frac{1}{1+x^2 y^2}=\frac{1}{\left(1+x^2\right)\left(1+y^2\right)}\frac{1}{1+x^2 y^2} \geq \frac{1}{\left(1+x^2\right)\left(1+y^2\right)}\left[\because 1+x^2 y^2 \leq 1+x^2+y^2+x^2 y^2\right]$
Hence, $f(x, y) \geq f(x) \cdot f(y)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $F: R \rightarrow R$ is a differentiable function and $f(3)=6$, then $\lim _{x \rightarrow 3} \int_6^{f(x)} \frac{2 t d t}{(x-2)}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let $I=\lim _{x \rightarrow 3} \int_6^{f(x)} \frac{2 t}{x-2} d t\left[\frac{0}{0}\right.$ form, as $\left.f(3)=6\right]$
On applying the L' Hospital rule, we get
$I=\lim _{x \rightarrow 3} \int_6^{f(x)} \frac{2 f(x) f^{\prime}(x)}{1}(\because f(3)=6)$
So, $I=3 f(3) \cdot f^{\prime}(3)=18 f^{\prime}(3)\therefore \quad \lim _{x \rightarrow 3} \int_6^{f(x)} \frac{2 t d t}{x-2}=18 f^{\prime}(3)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The value of $f(x)=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0}\left(\frac{8^x+2^x+4^x}{3}\right)^{2 / x}$, then $f(x)^{\prime}$ equals to
questions.solution:
$y=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0}\left(\frac{8^x+2^x+4^x}{3}\right)^{2 / x}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \log y=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{2}{x} \log \left(\frac{8^x+2^x+4^x}{3}\right) \\ & =2 \lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{1}{x}\left[\log \left(8^x+2^x+4^x\right)-\log 3\right]\end{aligned}=2 \lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{\left[\log \left(8^x+2^x+4^x\right)-\log 3\right]}{x} \quad\left[\frac{0}{0}\right.$ form $]$
On applying L' Hospital rule, we get
$\begin{aligned} & =2 \lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{\left[8^x \log 8+2^x \log 2+4^x \log 4\right]}{8^x+2^x+4^x} \\ & =2\left[\frac{\log 8+\log 2+\log 4}{3}\right]\end{aligned}=\frac{2}{3}[3 \log 2+\log 2+2 \log 2] \quad\left[\log (m)^n=n \log m\right]\begin{aligned} & =\frac{2}{3} \times 6 \log 2 \\ & \log y=4 \log 2=\log 16 \Rightarrow y=16\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $a^2, b^2$ and $c^2$ are in AP, then $b+c, c+a$ and $a+b$ are in $\qquad$
questions.solution:
We have, $a^2, b^2$ and $c^2$ are in AP adding $a b+b c+c a$ to each of these terms, we get $a^2+a b+b c+c a, b^2+a b+b c+c a$ and $c^2+a b+b c+c a$ are in AP.
$\Rightarrow(a+b)(a+c),(b+c)(b+a) \text { and }(c+a)(c+b)$ are in AP.
Dividing each term by $(b+c)(c+a)(a+b)$, we get
$\frac{1}{b+c}, \frac{1}{c+a}$ and $\frac{1}{a+b}$ are in AP
$\Rightarrow b+c, c+a$ and $a+b$ are in HP.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\sum_{i=1}^9\left(x_i-5\right)=9$ and $\sum_{i=1}^9\left(x_i-5\right)^2=45$, then the standard deviation of the 9 items $x_1, x_2 \ldots, x_9$ is
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \text { Given, } \sum_{i=1}^{\mathcal{y}}\left(x_i-5\right)=9 \\ & \sum x_i-45=9 \Rightarrow \sum x_i=54\end{aligned}$
Also, $\sum_{i=1}^9\left(x_i-5\right)^2=45\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow \quad & \sum x_i^2-10 \times 54+25 \times 9=45 \\ & \sum x_i^2=360\end{aligned}\therefore$ Standard deviation $(\sigma)=\sqrt{\frac{360}{9}-\left(\frac{54}{9}\right)^2}=2$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the line $\frac{x-1}{2}=\frac{y+1}{3}=\frac{z-1}{4}$ and $\frac{\boldsymbol{x}-3}{1}=\frac{\boldsymbol{y}-\boldsymbol{k}}{2}=\frac{z}{1}$ intersect, then $k$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given, two lines
$L_1: \frac{x-1}{2}=\frac{y+1}{3}=\frac{z-1}{4}$
and $L_2: \frac{x-3}{1}=\frac{y-k}{2}=\frac{z-0}{1}$
Let $L_1: \frac{x-1}{2}=\frac{y+1}{3}=\frac{z-1}{4}=p$
and $L_2: \frac{x-3}{1}=\frac{y-k}{2}=\frac{z-0}{1}=q$
Any point $P$ on line $L_1$ is of type
$P(2 p+1,3 p-1$ and $4 p+1)$ and any point $Q$ on the line $L_2$ is of type $Q(q+3,2 q+k$ and $q)$
Since, $L_1$ and $L_2$ are intersecting each other, hence, both point $P$ and $Q$ should coincide at the point of intersection. Corresponding co-ordinates of $P$ and $Q$ should be same.
$2 p+1=q+3,3 p-1=2 q+k \text { and } 4 p+1=q$
On solving, $2 p+1=q+3$ and $4 p+1=q$, we get
$p=-\frac{3}{2}$ and $q=-5$
On substituting the values of $p$ and $q$ in the third equation $3 p-1=2 q+k$, we get
$3\left(-\frac{3}{2}\right)-1=2(-5)+k\therefore \quad k=\frac{9}{2}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the foot of the perpendicular drawn from the point $(2,0,1)$ on a line passing through $(\alpha, 5,1)$ is $\left(\frac{7}{3}, \frac{5}{3}, \frac{15}{4}\right)$, then $\alpha$ is equal to_____
questions.solution:
It is given that $Q\left(\frac{7}{3}, \frac{5}{3}, \frac{15}{4}\right)$ is foot of perpendicular of point $P(2,0,1)$ to a line passes through point $A(\alpha, 5,1)$. So $P Q \perp A Q$
$\because$ Direction ratios of line segments $P Q$ is $\left(\frac{7}{3}, \frac{5}{3}, \frac{15}{4}\right)$ and direction ratios of line $A Q$ is $\left(\alpha-\frac{7}{3}, \frac{10}{3},-\frac{11}{4}\right)$ Since, $P Q$ and $A Q$ is perpendicular to each other, $\text { so } P Q \cdot A Q=0\frac{7}{3}\left(\alpha-\frac{7}{3}\right)+\frac{5}{3} \times \frac{10}{3}+\frac{15}{4} \times\left(-\frac{11}{4}\right)=0\Rightarrow \quad \frac{7(3 \alpha-7)}{9}+\frac{50}{9}-\frac{165}{16}=0\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \quad \frac{336 \alpha-784+800-1485}{144}=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad 336 \alpha=1469 \Rightarrow \alpha=\frac{1469}{336}=4.372\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the vectors $p=(a+1) \hat{\mathbf{i}}+a \hat{\mathbf{j}}+a \hat{\mathbf{k}}$, $q=a \hat{\mathbf{i}}+(a+1) \hat{\mathbf{j}}+a \hat{\mathbf{k}}$ and $r=a \hat{\mathbf{i}}+a \hat{\mathbf{j}}+(a+1) \hat{\mathbf{k}}(a \in R)$ are coplanar, then the value of $a$ is____
questions.solution:
Given, vectors are
$\begin{aligned} & \mathbf{p}=(a+1) \hat{\mathbf{i}}+a \hat{\mathbf{j}}+a \hat{\mathbf{k}} \\ & \mathbf{q}=a \hat{\mathbf{i}}+(a+1) \hat{\mathbf{j}}+a \hat{\mathbf{k}}\end{aligned}$
and $\mathbf{r}=a \hat{\mathbf{i}}+a \hat{\mathbf{j}}+(a+1) \hat{\mathbf{k}}[p q r]=0\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow\left|\begin{array}{ccc}a+1 & a & a \\ a & a+1 & a \\ a & a & a+1\end{array}\right|=0 \\ & \Rightarrow(a+1)\left[(a+1)^2-a^2\right]-a\left[a(a+1)-a^2\right] \\ & \quad+a\left[a^2-a(a+1)\right]=0\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow(a+1)[2 a+1]-2 a[a]=0 \\ & \Rightarrow 2 a^2+3 a+1-2 a^2=0 \\ & \Rightarrow a=-\frac{1}{3}=-0.33\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Ionisation potential of hydrogen atom is 13.6 V . Hydrogen atoms in the ground state are excited by monochromatic radiation of photon energy 12.1 eV . The spectral lines emitted by hydrogen atoms according to Bohr's theory will be

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A charged capacitor when filled with a dielectric $K=3$ has charge $Q_0$, voltage $V_0$ and field $E_0$. If the dielectric is replaced with another one having $K=9$, the new values of charge voltage and field will be respectively
questions.solution:
When charging battery is disconnected then charge remains constant, $V$ becomes $1 / K$ times and $E$ becomes $1 / K$ times.
So, new value of charge is $Q_0$.
New value of $V=\frac{V_0 \times 3}{9}=\frac{V_0}{3}$
New value of $E=\frac{E_0 \times 3}{9}=\frac{E_0}{3}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The resistance of a wire at $20^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ is $20 \Omega$ and at $500^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ is $60 \Omega$. At which temperature its resistance will be $25 \Omega$ ?
questions.solution:
Resistance, $R_t=R_0(1+\alpha t)20=R_0(1+20 \alpha) \text { and } 60=R_0(1+500 \alpha)$
From this equation, we can find
$\begin{aligned} R_0 & =18.33 \Omega \\ \alpha & =4.54 \times 10^{-3} \\ R_t & =25 \Omega\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}& \text { Again, } \quad R_t=R_0(1+\alpha t) \\
& 25=18.33\left(1+4.54 \times 10^{-3} t\right)\end{aligned}\text { We find } t=80^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$

The value of work function of the barium is ........ eV. . given, $\left.\frac{e}{m}=1.7 \times 10^{11}\right)$

Radius of circular path described by a charged particle in a magnetic field B is given by
$r=\sqrt{\frac{2 m K}{q B}} \Rightarrow K=\frac{q^2 B^2 r^2}{2 m}=\left(\frac{e}{m}\right) \frac{e B^2 r^2}{2}$
where, $K=$ kinetic energy of a particle
$q=$ charge on a particle
$r=$ radius of circular path
$=\frac{1}{2} \times 1.7 \times 10^{11} \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \times\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{17}} \times 10^{-5}\right)^2 \times(1)^2=8 \times 10^{-20} \mathrm{~J}=0.5 \mathrm{eV}$
Using the relation,

where, $E=h v=\frac{h c}{\lambda}=\frac{12375}{\lambda(\text { in } Å)}=\left(\frac{12375}{2475}\right) \mathrm{eV}-0.5 \mathrm{eV}=4.5 \mathrm{eV}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A proton accelerated through a potential difference of 100 V , has de-Broglie wavelength $\lambda_0$. The de-Broglie wavelength of an $\alpha$-particle, accelerated through 800 V is
questions.solution: As, $\lambda=\frac{h}{\sqrt{2 q V m}} \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{q V m}}\begin{array}{ll}\therefore & \frac{\lambda_\alpha}{\lambda_p}=\sqrt{\frac{q_p V_p m_p}{q_\alpha V_\alpha m_\alpha}}=\sqrt{\frac{1 \times 100 \times 1}{2 \times 800 \times 4}}=\frac{1}{8} \\ \therefore & \lambda_\alpha=\frac{\lambda_p}{8}=\frac{\lambda_0}{8}\end{array}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A vertical disc of diameter 10 cm makes 20 revolutions per second about a horizontal axis passing through its centre. A uniform magnetic field $10^{-1} \mathrm{~T}$ acts perpendicular to the plane of the disc. If the potential difference between its centre and rim is found to be $\frac{\pi}{x} \times 10^{-p}$ Volt, then find the ratio of $x / p$.
questions.solution:
As we know, disc is equivalent to a rod of length $r$. Divide disc into rods, each rod can be replaced by a battery and these batteries are would be paralial in arrangement.
According to the question, radius of disc, $r=\frac{10}{2}=5 \mathrm{~cm}=0.05 \mathrm{~m}$ Angular velocity, $\omega=20 \times 2 \pi=40 \pi \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}$ Magnetic field, $B=10^{-1} \mathrm{~T}$ The emf of a disc is given as $e=\frac{1}{2} B \omega r^2=\frac{1}{2}\left(10^{-1}\right)(40 \pi)(0.05)^2\Rightarrow \quad V_0-V_A=1.57 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{~V}=\frac{\pi}{2} \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{~V}=\frac{\pi}{x} \times 10^{-p} \mathrm{~V}$ (given) $\therefore \quad \frac{x}{p}=\frac{2}{2}=1$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The acceleration due to gravity becomes $g / 2$ ( $g=$ acceleration due to gravity on the surface of the earth) at a height equals to
questions.solution:
The acceleration due to gravity,
$g=\frac{G M}{R^2}\ldots$ (i)
At a height $h$ above the surface of the earth, the acceleration due to gravity is
$g^{\prime}=\frac{G M}{(R+h)^2}\ldots$ (ii)
From Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get
$\frac{g}{g^{\prime}}=\left(\frac{R+h}{R}\right)^2=\left(1+\frac{h}{R}\right)^2\Rightarrow \quad \frac{g^{\prime}}{g^{\prime}}=\left(1+\frac{h}{R}\right)^{-2}=\left(1-\frac{2 h}{R}\right)^2$
Here,
$g^{\prime}=\frac{g}{2}\therefore \quad \frac{g / 2}{g}=\left(1-\frac{2 h}{R}\right) \Rightarrow \frac{2 h}{R}=\frac{1}{2}$ or $h=\frac{R}{4}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
The lower end of a capillary tube is dipped into water and it is seen that water rises through 7.5 cm in the capillary. Given, surface tension of water is $7.5 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{Nm}^{-1}$ and angle of contact between water and glass capillary tube is zero.
What will be the diameter (in mm ) of the capillary tube? (given, $g=10 \mathrm{~ms}^{-2}$ )
questions.solution:
Given, $h=7.5 \mathrm{~cm}=7.5 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{~m}\begin{aligned}& S=7.5 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{Nm}^{-1} \\
& \theta=\sigma^{\circ}, r=?\end{aligned}$
As, $h=\frac{2 S \cos \theta}{r \rho g} \Rightarrow 2 r=\frac{4 S \cos \theta}{h \rho g}=\frac{4 \times 7.5 \times 10^{-2} \times \cos 0^{\circ}}{7.5 \times 10^{-2} \times 10^3 \times 10}=4 \times 10^{-4}=0.4 \mathrm{~mm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two steel wires having same length are suspended from a ceiling under the same load. If the ratio of their energy stored per unit volume is $1: 4$, then the ratio of their diameters is found to be $\sqrt{k}: 1$. Find the value of $k$.
questions.solution:
Elastic potential energy stored in a loaded'wire,
$U=\frac{1}{2} \times($ Stress \times  Strain \times  Volume $)\therefore$ Energy stored per unit volume,
$U=\frac{U}{\text { Volume }}=\frac{1}{2} \times$ Stress \times  Strain $=\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{F}{A}\right)^2 \times \frac{1}{Y}\frac{U_A}{U_B}=\frac{\frac{1}{2 Y} \cdot \frac{F^2}{A_A^2}}{\frac{1}{2 Y} \cdot \frac{F^2}{A_B^2}}=\frac{A_B^2}{A_A^2}, \frac{U_A}{U_B}=\frac{d_B^4}{d_A^4}$
Here,$\frac{U_A}{U_B}=\frac{1}{4}, \frac{d_B^4}{d_A^4}=\frac{1}{4}$ or $\frac{d_B}{d_A}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\frac{d_A}{d_B}=\sqrt{2}: 1=\sqrt{k}: 1$ (given)
$\therefore \quad k=2$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two stones having different masses $m_1$ and $m_2$ are projected at angles $\theta$ and $\left(90^{\circ}-\theta\right)$ with same velocity from the same point. The ratio of their maximum heights is
questions.solution:
Maximum height, $H_1=\frac{u^2 \sin ^2 \theta}{2 g}\ldots$ (i)
and $H_2=\frac{u^2 \sin ^2\left(90^{\circ}-\theta\right)}{2 g}\ldots$ (ii)
From Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get
$\frac{H_1}{H_2}=\frac{\sin ^2 \theta}{\sin ^2\left(90^{\circ}-\theta\right)}, \frac{H_1}{H_2}=\frac{\tan ^2 \theta}{1}\therefore \quad H_1: H_2=\tan ^2 \theta: 1$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A function of time is represented as follows $\sin \omega t+\cos 2 \omega t+\sin 4 \omega t$. The motion represented by it is
questions.solution:
This is an example of a periodic motion. It can be noted that each term represents a periodic function with different angular frequency. Since, period is the least interval of time after which a function repeats its value, $\sin \omega t$ has a period
$T_0=\frac{2 \pi}{\omega}\cos 2 \omega t$ has a period $\frac{\pi}{\omega}=\frac{T_0}{2}$ and $\sin 4 \omega t$ has a period $\frac{2 \pi}{4 \omega}=\frac{T_0}{4}$
The period of the first term is a multiple of the periods of the last two terms. Therefore, the smallest interval of time after which the sum of the three terms repeats is $T_0$ and thus, the sum is a periodic function with a period $\frac{2 \pi}{\omega}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A disc of mass 5 kg and radius 50 cm rolls on the ground at the rate of $10 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$. Find the kinetic energy of the disc in J .
questions.solution:
Here, mass of the disc, $M=5 \mathrm{~kg}$
Radius of the disc, $R=50 \mathrm{~cm}=1 / 2 \mathrm{~m}$ Linear velocity of the disc, $v=10 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$ 
As,  $\quad v=R \omega\therefore \quad 10=\frac{1}{2} \omega$ or $\omega=10 \times 2=20 \mathrm{rad} \mathrm{s}^{-1}$
Also, moment of inertia of disc about an axis through its centre,
$I=\frac{1}{2} M R^2=\frac{1}{2} \times 5 \times\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2=\frac{5}{8} \mathrm{~kg}^2-\mathrm{m}\begin{aligned} & \therefore \mathrm{KE} \text { of translation }=\frac{1}{2} m v^2=\frac{1}{2} \times 5 \times(10)^2=250 \mathrm{~J} \\ & \text { Rotational kinetic energy }=\frac{1}{2} / \omega^2=\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{5}{8}\right)(20)^2=125 \mathrm{~J}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} \text { Total kinetic energy } & =\text { Translational }+ \text { Rotational } \\ & =(250+125)=375 \mathrm{~J}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In Young's double slit experiment, if the source of light changes from orange to blue, then
options: the central bright fringe will become a dark fringe
the distance between consecutive fringes will decrease
the distance between consecutive fringes will increase.
the intensity of the minima will increase.
questions.solution:
We know that in Young's double slit experiment, fringe width $\beta=\frac{D \lambda}{d}, \beta \propto \lambda$
Since, $\lambda_{\text {blue }} \lt \lambda_{\text {orange }}$
Thus, $\beta_{\text {blue }} \lt \beta_{\text {orange }}\therefore$ In Young's double slit experiment, if the source of light changes from orange to blue, then distance between the consecutive fringes will decrease.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A force $F=(2+x)$ acts on a particle in $x$-direction, where F is in newton and $x$ in metre. The work done by this force during'a displacement from $x=1.0 \mathrm{~m}$ to $x=2.0 \mathrm{~m}$ is
questions.solution:
The work done in small displacement from $x$ to $x+d x$ is
$d W=F d x=(2+x) d x$
Hence,
$W=\int_1^2 d W=\int_1^2(2+x) d x=\int_1^2 2 d x+\int_1^2 x d x=\left[2 x+\frac{x^2}{2}\right]_1^2=3.5 \mathrm{~J}$
